fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that inserts the words "or streptomycin" into the heading and first sentence of an existing provision. The tempting reading is that the underlying section 507 may involve regulations on drug certification, but nothing in this text itself authorizes rulemaking, consultation, hearings, advisory bodies, or suits involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: the first sentence of subsection (a) of such section 507 is amended by inserting “or streptomycin” after “penicillin”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute, simply adding the word 'streptomycin' to existing text. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely legislative drafting.
qwen_block.s: The heading of section 507 of such Act, as amended, is amended by inserting “or streptomycin” after “ penicillin ”; and the first sentence of subsection (a) of such section 507 is amended by inserting “or streptomycin” after “penicillin”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that adds 'or streptomycin' to the heading and first sentence of section 507. The text itself does not require or authorize rulemaking, public comment, a hearing, an advisory body, or consultation with anyone outside the federal government. Any rulemaking authority would have to come from the unquoted text of the underlying section, not from this section, so the 'Yes' reading relies on outside knowledge rather than the language being labelled.
opus.s: the first sentence of subsection (a) of such section 507 is amended by inserting “or streptomycin” after “penicillin”.
opus.b: **Label: No.** The tempting reading is "Yes": section 507 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act sets up a regulation-based program for certifying penicillin batches. By adding streptomycin, this amendment arguably extends a rulemaking authority, and the definition counts rulemaking as participation. That reading fails because the text shown never mentions regulations, comment periods, hearings, consultation or any party outside the federal government. It only makes a word-level insertion. The "Yes" reading depends on my recollection of what section 507 says, not on anything this text states, so my confidence is moderate.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a legislative amendment that modifies the text of a previous statute to include streptomycin. It does not establish any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory committees, public comment periods, or consultation requirements mentioned.
qwen_chat.s: The heading of section 507 of such Act, as amended, is amended by inserting “or streptomycin” after “penicillin”; and the first sentence of subsection (a) of such section 507 is amended by inserting “or streptomycin” after “penicillin”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending a statute regarding drugs implies some form of public consultation or regulatory process. However, the text itself is purely a legislative amendment instruction, changing the text of a previous law to include "streptomycin" alongside "penicillin." It does not describe any process of consulting with outsiders, holding hearings, or creating advisory bodies. It is a substantive change to the law, not a procedural requirement for participation.
